summary_rationale: NBIL (GraniteShares 2x Long NBIS Daily ETF) fails fundamental compounding standards on two independent layers. First, as a 1940 Act daily-reset single-stock ETF, NBIL's audited N-CSR and Oct 28, 2026 497K filings disclose a 1.41% net operating expense ratio (1.50% cap), an additional 1.45% estimated indirect swap cost, 100% single-counterparty concentration with Clear Street, LLC at an audited OBFR01 + 600 bps swap financing rate, and quadratic daily volatility decay—while AUM contracted 68% from $195.60M (June 30, 2026) to $62.26M (Nov 2026) behind larger, lower-fee multi-dealer rivals NEBX (1.30%, $353.37M) and NBIG (0.76%, $90.37M). Second, the underlying business, Nebius Group N.V. (NBIS), while scaling Q3 2026 revenue to $980.8M (70% concentrated in three customers; 85% of $4.04B accounts receivable in two customers) on >$40B–$46B of backlog, remains deeply FCF-negative (-$3,664.1M FY2025; -$15.43B 9M 2026 CapEx; ~$27B FY2026E; $40B–$45B FY2027E). Q3 2026 footnotes further reveal that Q3's +$50.4M GAAP operating income relied on a $325.1M one-time partnership item and a Jan 1, 2026 server depreciation extension from 4 to 5 years (+$43.1M Q3 / +$129.2M 9M boost), alongside $16.48B principal debt, the Oct 22 $3.5B Citi facility, $13.86B uncommenced leases, $2.73B fixed power commitments, $1.46B VIE exposure, +15.8% YTD share dilution (to 292.90M shares + 21.07M NVIDIA warrants), and $196.5M 9M SBC (+237% YoY). Operational KPIs (backlog, >4 GW contracted power, Q3 revenue scale) warrant PASS_WITH_WATCH due to CapEx escalation, colocation delays, useful-life accounting changes, and ARR-guidance retirement, while NBIL itself remains structurally unsuitable as a long-term fundamental holding.
